core_fields.description: This project seek to empowers smallholder farmers cooperatives in Nimba County, through climate-smart agriculture, sustainable seedling and land-use interventions. Enhancing effort for access to nutritional food, creating market access, reducing post-harvest losses through storage facilities, and promoting seedling conservation and development, GERAD aim to enhance food security, resilience to climate change, and livelihoods. The project further seek to empower women and youth with improve knowledge on productivity, ensuring long-term environmental sustainability and farmers income.
core_fields.abstract: Smallholder farmers in Nimba county, Liberia faces serious challenges like low soil fertility, climate stress, post-harvest losses associated with poor seedling conservation and development, and limited market access, that post threat on food security and local livelihoods for vulnerable women and youth. To address these issues, the propose intervention will target climate-smart agriculture and restoration/regenerative activities. Climate smart agriculture Training will be tailor to farmers on restoration through agroforestry approach. This approach will enable farmers have basic understanding on environmental management and land-use planning. In an effort to reduce post-harvest looses, which is a major challenge to be targeted, the proposed intervention seek to enhance food quality through the construction of eco-cool storage facilities and the installation of solar dryers for seeds conservation. The intervention is integrated with local and modern farming techniques through diversify approaches, including seed varieties, organic composting, and reduction in CO2 emission. Understanding that price analysis is a major challenge, the project seek to establish digital platform through farmers -connect program. this will help strengthen collaboration between smallholder cooperative and aggregators for a fair and accessible market. The intervention impact will be achieve in a very significant ways by reducing food looses, and improving smallholders income generation opportunity. The project will target women, youth, and person living with disabilities through training and VSLA activities through cooperative engagement and impactful transformation. This intervention will sustainably restore loose ecosystem and create resilience for adaptation to mitigate the impacts of climate change, promote carbon sequestration, and improve food security.

core_fields.title: Restoring the Land: Indigenous Climate Solutions for Food and Livelihood Renewal
core_fields.description: Plan Conservation creates Indigenous-led conservation plans recognized by both federal and tribal governments, allowing Navajo families to legally farm and graze. Using Navajo knowledge and modern mapping, we restore soil, capture water, and rebuild food systems once lost to drought and bureaucracy. Each plan transforms years of waiting into one day of approval, restoring land, food security, and sovereignty across the Navajo Nation.
core_fields.abstract: This innovation restores agricultural access through Indigenous-led conservation planning that unites modern mapping with traditional Navajo knowledge. For decades, Navajo families have faced barriers to reclaiming ancestral farmland and grazing areas because of complex regulations and outdated government systems. Many permits, once issued between the 1940s and early 2000s, are now cancelled or frozen without a current conservation plan, making legal land use impossible for farming or livestock ownership. Plan Conservation resolves this challenge through a one-day process that develops federally and tribally recognized conservation plans required to activate permits for agricultural and grazing use. The approach combines ecological site data, GIS mapping, and cultural knowledge that interprets soil, water flow, and vegetation as living indicators of balance. Each plan equips families with tools to restore their land, manage drought, and rebuild soil and water systems through regenerative, low-cost conservation practices. It also creates a foundation for future funding, connecting each family to opportunities for USDA, NGO, and tribal support. The immediate benefit is the legal restoration of access to ancestral lands. The lasting benefit is a resilient system where Navajo families can grow food, graze livestock, and sustain income within their communities. This innovation transforms bureaucratic delay into empowerment, restoring land, livelihoods, and hope for generations who deserve to live, grow, and thrive on their land once again.

core_fields.title: AI-Driven Biodegradable Carbon Sink Planters for Regenerative Agriculture and Climate-Resilient Food Systems in Drylands
core_fields.description: Soil Doctors patented AI-Driven Carbon Sink Planter is a biodegradable, self-decaying device designed to grow trees and crops in dry, degraded lands. It releases nutrients over time, forming a fertile ring around roots to enable intercropping and boost survival above 85%. Powered by AI and soil sensors, it reduces water use by over 50%, regenerates soils, enhances carbon sequestration, and strengthens climate-resilient, nutrition-secure food systems for smallholder farmers.
core_fields.abstract: In dry and degraded lands, food and tree production are limited by soil infertility, moisture stress, and high seedling mortality threatening food security, biodiversity, and livelihoods. Soil Doctors' patented AI-Driven Carbon Sink Planter addresses this challenge through an intelligent, regenerative technology that restores soil health while enabling trees and crops to thrive under extreme conditions. The biodegradable planter decays naturally over time, forming a nutrient-rich ring around the root zone that retains moisture, stimulates microbial activity, and provides slow-release nutrients. This design reduces water use by over 50% and ensures seedling survival rates above 85%, even in arid zones. The planter composition integrates biochar, compost, and organic binders, making it both eco-friendly and circular. AI and soil sensor data inform planting density, water scheduling, and soil amendments, optimizing growth and carbon sequestration potential. This data-driven feedback loop enables farmers to manage resources efficiently, increase yields, and improve resilience to droughts and climate shocks. The innovation was developed through insights in soil ecology, circular bioeconomy, and regenerative agriculture, combining traditional composting knowledge with modern AI analytics. Immediate benefits include higher crop productivity, reduced input costs, and improved food and income security. Long-term impacts include enhanced soil organic carbon, restored ecosystems, and climate-resilient food systems across the Global South. By empowering smallholder farmers, communities, and schools to restore degraded soils, Soil Doctors' Carbon Sink Planter accelerates the transition toward equitable, sustainable, and regenerative food production.

core_fields.title: Solar-Powered Smart Agri-Tech Pilot: An Off-Grid Blueprint for Ugandan Farms
core_fields.description: Sustainable Access Foundation (U.S.-based 501c3) and Bandera Farmers Network International (Uganda) are piloting a low-cost, solar-powered smart irrigation system. This off-grid project addresses severe water scarcity, which causes crop failure. We are using IoT sensors and mobile controls to optimize water usage, increase yields, and improve farmer livelihoods. This $25,000 "seed" project will prove an affordable and scalable blueprint, designed to empower smallholder farmers across Africa.
core_fields.abstract: What problem is being solved, why is it relevant? Ugandan farming collectives, like our partner BAFANI, are critically vulnerable to crop failure during increasingly long and severe dry seasons. This is relevant because it directly threatens food security and economic stability for thousands of smallholder farmers. Manual, flood irrigation methods are labor-intensive, waste scarce water, and unreliable grid power makes most modern tech solutions unfeasible. How is the problem being solved? We are deploying a low-cost, fully solar-powered "Smart Agri-Tech Kit." This system uses IoT soil sensors and micro-weather stations to gather real-time data. Farmers receive simple alerts on basic mobile devices (e.g., "Zone 2 is dry") and can remotely start or stop irrigation valves. The entire system runs off-grid. What... insight led to this particular solution? The key insight is that existing smart irrigation systems are technically and financially inaccessible to smallholder farmers; they are designed for large, wealthy, industrial farms. Our insight is that by co-designing a system with farmers and prioritizing affordability and off-grid autonomy, we can use mature, available tech (IoT, solar) to build a durable, low-cost kit. This proves climate resilience is achievable for low-resource collectives. What are specific immediate and sustainable benefits...? Immediate benefits for farmers include: 1) Drastically reduced water waste, 2) Lowered labor hours, and 3) Increased crop yields. This creates greater food security and economic empowerment for their communities. The sustainable benefit for the environment is a replicable, fully off-grid blueprint that provides climate resilience for the entire region.

core_fields.title: Functional Biodegradable Mulch Films
core_fields.description: This project develops natural, functional, biodegradable mulch sheets to replace conventional polyethylene films. Using composite biopolymers, agricultural biowaste and soil-enriching microbial consortia and/or nutrients. The sheets are fabricated through innovative process involving casting/electrospinning/extrusion technologies. The study addresses plastic-removal challenges, soil microplastic pollution and sustaining soil microbiome. The resulting mulch aims to improve crop performance, reduce weed growth, enhance soil health, and eliminate disposal costs, contributing to more sustainable agricultural practices.
core_fields.abstract: This project introduces a new generation of functional biodegradable mulch sheets made from natural polymer based composite materials reinforced with organic fillers, stabilizers, UV absorbers, and plasticizers. Unlike conventional polyethylene films, which are difficult to collect, recycle, and often leave long-lasting microplastic residues in soil, these mulch sheets are fully biodegradable and environmentally compatible. They also address limitations of current commercial biodegradable mulches, such as PLA or PBAT, which remain expensive. The innovation lies in combining natural polymer composites with agricultural biowaste, bioactive soil microbial consortia/nutrients, a feature rarely integrated into existing mulch technologies. These microorganisms include selected degraders and soil enrichers that accelerate the breakdown of the mulch while the nutrients simultaneously improve soil fertility. Process innovation in fabrication methods such as membrane casting and electrospinning/extrusion further support sustainability. The resulting sheets are engineered for sufficient strength and UV stability during crop growth, followed by controlled biodegradation in the soil. By replacing persistent plastics with degradable, soil-enriching alternatives, this innovation provides immediate benefits such as reduced labor for removal, improved soil structure and moisture retention, reduced weed growth, and potentially higher yields. Sustained benefits extend to cleaner soils, better food quality, lower pollution, and long-term economic and environmental gains for farmers, communities, and ecosystems.

core_fields.abstract: SAFE AgriBassa introduces a community-driven innovation that integrates low-literacy digital traceability tools, climate-smart agriculture practices, and agribusiness market linkages to address unsafe pesticide use, soil degradation, and market exclusion in rural Liberia. Many smallholder farmers face harmful chemical practices, declining soil fertility, and the absence of record-keeping and traceability systems, limiting access to premium markets and compromising food safety. Through agribusiness fairs and market days, farmers will connect with hotels, supermarkets, and agro-processors, strengthening visibility and demand for safe, locally produced food. core_fields.title: Waste to Value Circular Agribusiness for Regenerative Food Production
core_fields.description: Our project transforms agricultural waste and swine manure into clean energy, organic fertilisers, and nutritious pork products through an integrated circular agribusiness model. Using existing land, infrastructure, and strong community partnerships, it delivers regenerative food production, reduced environmental impact, and improved rural livelihoods. This low-risk, high-impact model strengthens Angolas food systems while demonstrating a scalable, replicable blueprint for circular agriculture across Africa.
core_fields.abstract: Angola was once a major agricultural producer, but decades of conflict and underinvestment left vast arable land unused and domestic production capacity severely underdeveloped. Today, the country imports most of its food, faces persistent protein gaps, and lacks local processing capacity. Meanwhile, thousands of tons of agricultural residues and organic waste remain unutilised, contributing to environmental degradation and rural economic stagnation. Our innovation introduces an integrated waste-to-value circular agribusiness model that combines diversified vegetable cultivation with a vertically integrated swine production system. The model uses on-farm crop residues and swine manure as feedstock for a biodigester that converts up to 1,500 tons of organic waste annually into clean biogas for energy and over 1,000 tons of high-quality organic fertiliser. These inputs significantly reduce production costs, regenerate soils, and close nutrient loops while enabling reliable, year-round food production. The system yields multiple value-added products: fresh pork, cured meat, homemade sausages, organic fertilisers, and renewable energy, enhancing profitability and resilience. By integrating biogas, composting, animal production, and crop cultivation, the model provides a cost-efficient, climate-smart solution that enhances food availability, reduces emissions, and increases rural employment. This approach is novel in Angola, where circular farming and integrated bio-resource valorisation remain rare. It demonstrates how local bio-waste can be transformed into energy and regenerative inputs while strengthening nutrition and economic stability. This validated model is designed for scalable replication across Angola and other African regions, offering a practical pathway toward regenerative, circular, and economically viable food systems.

core_fields.title: BioGel: Scalable Biological Infrastructure for Regenerative and Climate-Resilient Food Systems
core_fields.description: Our innovative BioGel, is a patented gel-based biological delivery platform designed to address the inconsistent performance and limited adoption of conventional agricultural biologicals. BioGel enables high-density microbial delivery, extended shelf life, and controlled release while remaining compatible with existing farming practices. Deployed across crops and regions, the platform reduces chemical fertilizer use, improves soil health, and delivers measurable economic benefits to farmers, positioning it as scalable technology and process for resilient food systems.
core_fields.abstract: Agricultural systems globally face soil degradation, declining nutrient use efficiency, and increasing dependence on chemical fertilizers that raise production costs, environmental emissions, and long-term vulnerability of food systems. Although biological inputs are promoted as alternatives, their adoption remains limited due to short shelf life, low microbial survival, variable field performance, and operational complexity for farmers. 1000 Farms addresses this challenge through BioGel, a patented gel-based biological delivery infrastructure that improves the reliability and scalability of agricultural biologicals. BioGel encapsulates high-density microbial consortia within a natural polymeric gel matrix that protects microorganisms during storage and application and enables controlled release in the rhizosphere. Compared with conventional liquid, powder, or granulated biologicals, BioGel supports significantly higher microbial payloads, extended shelf stability, and ultra-low, water-soluble application doses that integrate seamlessly into existing fertilizer and irrigation systems. The innovation is based on interdisciplinary insights from microbiology, biochemistry, materials science, soil biology, and agronomy, recognizing that biological inputs fail at scale primarily due to delivery and performance variability rather than microbial strain limitations. By addressing delivery, BioGel enables biologicals to function as reliable agricultural inputs rather than niche supplements. Immediate benefits include improved nutrient use efficiency, reduced fertilizer consumption, improved soil moisture retention, and yield stability. Over time, BioGel contributes to soil regeneration, reduced greenhouse gas emissions, improved resilience to climate stress, and economically viable pathways to regenerative agriculture without disrupting current food production systems.

core_fields.title: Transforming Organic Waste into Sustainable Protein and Fertilizer for Ugandan Farmers
core_fields.description: Our project converts organic and agro-processing waste into high-protein Black Soldier Fly (BSF) insect meal and organic fertilizer, providing affordable, sustainable inputs for Ugandan smallholder farmers. By scaling BSF production, we reduce waste pollution, lower feed costs by 20 30%, improve soil fertility, and strengthen farmer livelihoods. The project creates green jobs for youth and women while advancing circular agroecology and climate resilience in Uganda.
core_fields.abstract: Uganda faces two interconnected challenges: rapidly growing volumes of organic waste that pollute the environment, and high animal feed and fertilizer costs that limit the productivity of smallholder farmers. Fishmeal and soy the main protein sources for animal feed are increasingly expensive and environmentally unsustainable, while soil depletion continues to reduce crop yields. Our innovation uses Black Soldier Fly (BSF) bioconversion technology to transform organic and agro-processing waste into high-protein insect meal for livestock and nutrient-rich organic fertilizer for crops. BSF larvae naturally consume large quantities of organic waste and convert it into valuable biomass, making them an efficient, climate-smart alternative to conventional feed production. The scientific insight behind this solution is the BSF larva s exceptional ability to convert waste into protein with minimal water, land, or energy. Compared to soy or fishmeal, BSF production emits far fewer greenhouse gases and requires no arable land. Our technical process involves controlled breeding, waste preprocessing, larval growing, drying, and milling producing consistent, high-quality feed and fertilizer. This innovation directly benefits farmers by reducing feed costs by 20 30%, improving animal growth rates, and restoring soil fertility. Communities benefit from reduced waste pollution, cleaner urban environments, and new green jobs, especially for youth and women. The environment gains through lower methane emissions, reduced pressure on fish stocks and forests, and circular use of local resources.

core_fields.title: Thriving Zimbabwean communities enjoying food sovereignty, resilient farmer-led seed systems and vibrant agroecological landscapes
core_fields.description: ZIMSOFF works with smallholder farmers in Zimbabwe to advocate for food sovereignty through farmer-led, agroecological approaches. The organization promotes a transition to sustainable food systems by connecting farmers with CSOs, universities, and government through emerging centers of excellence on agroecology. This framework supports traditional knowledge and innovative techniques for seed, food, and farming to improve livelihoods and build resilient food systems.
core_fields.abstract: Current promoters of food and nutrition are not including social and cultural dimensions of territorial food systems that are linked to grassroots movements for food sovereignty within traditional governance structures. This concentration of power in food and farming systems by the conventional narrative is still locking it in the industrial logic, posing immense barriers to social and cultural transition. This is creating a tension between efforts at convergence of food system innovations from below that have notable positive results, versus co-optation of grassroots cultures and practices by private and public actors who are committed not to changing the logic of industrial agriculture, but instead to reducing its harm. ZIMSOFF has identified 240 farming families and is supporting them to build their capability to develop their family farms to become learning centers of excellence for agroecology and food sovereignty. ZIMSOFF is supporting them to develop confidence to facilitate farmer to farmer learning and exchanges using their living examples. By actively self-organizing and participating they are becoming change-makers. The smallholder farmers, in turn, are influencing other neighboring communities, and once enough communities have changed their way of thinking, there can be mass mobilization to influence mind-sets and thus starting to shift a society in the broader sense and influencing policies that support agroecology, food sovereignty and healthy eating. The emerging centers of excellence on agroecology and food sovereignty are providing a framework for high understanding levels for the transition to sustainable food systems in Zimbabwe connecting smallholder farmers, CSOs, Universities and Government.

core_fields.title: Circular Duckweed Systems for Localized, Sustainable, Animal Feed Production
core_fields.description: Feed in Pakistan is expensive and mostly imported soy, which hurts farmers and the environment. Ful grows duckweed, a local, fast-growing aquatic plant that replaces soy as a high-protein feed. It uses wastewater and little land, making it far more resource-efficient and climate-resilient for a water-scarce country. Our goal is to build local feed independence while reducing costs, emissions, and reliance on imported crops.
core_fields.abstract: Livestock feed in Pakistan depends heavily on imported soybean meal, which is expensive, emission-intensive, and vulnerable to global price shocks. This dependency limits farmer profitability and contributes to deforestation and high feed-related carbon footprints. Ful's innovation replaces imported soy with locally grown duckweed: a small aquatic plant rich in protein and amino acids. Using modular open-pond systems, we cultivate duckweed on non-arable land using nutrient runoff and wastewater, turning waste into value. These systems produce feed with minimal inputs, recycle nutrients that would otherwise pollute waterways, and operate year-round even in arid regions. The concept builds on circular bioeconomy and wastewater-phytoremediation research showing that duckweed doubles its biomass in 48 hours while removing nitrogen and phosphorus from water. Ful adapted this insight into a scalable on-farm system that produces one ton of wet biomass weekly at less than half the cost of soy meal. Field trials have shown 48 % higher egg yields in layers, faster livestock fattening, and very low aflatoxin levels (3.8 ppb), making it ideal for dairy use. Methane-reduction impact will be scientifically quantified through controlled lab trials at NUST (Dr. Chattha) alongside ongoing work with ARID and UVAS. Immediate benefits include lower feed costs, improved animal performance, and higher farmer income. Sustainable benefits include reduced water pollution, lower import dependency, and a climate-resilient feed supply chain that cuts both emissions and foreign-exchange losses. Ful's approach turns nutrient waste into circular, low-carbon agricultural growth.

core_fields.title: The Resilient Smallholder: Hyperlocal Advisories and Equitable Market Access for Sustainable Farming
core_fields.description: FarmIT is an integrated digital platform offering bundled services to Kenya's smallholder farmers. We combine pest and disease diagnosis, hyperlocal climate-smart advisory, and direct market access into one solution. This addresses core challenges of low yields and unfair pricing, helping farmers reduce waste, increase productivity and income, and build climate resilience all through a single, accessible service.
core_fields.abstract: Smallholder farmers are the cornerstone of Kenya's food security and economic independence. A remarkable 80% of our nation's food supply is grown by their hands. Their contribution is foundational, generating 35% of Kenya's GDP and employing 70% of our rural population. However, their yields decline yearly. According to KNBS (2021), 86% of smallholder farmers lack knowledge of sustainable agricultural practices. They face unpredictable weather, unknown pests and diseases. Through guesswork, they misuse inputs like fertilizer and water, leading to stunted crops, failed harvests, and environmental pollution.After all this, they are still forced to sell to middlemen at unfair and exploitative prices. These challenges are not just agricultural, they are systemic and deeply human. FarmIT has developed an integrated digital platform that directly addresses the core challenges facing smallholder farmers in Kenya. Our solution combines precision farming advisory with direct market access through three key components. The Sensei tool enables farmers to instantly diagnose pests and diseases through photo recognition, providing treatment recommendations and connecting them to nearby agro-vets. Crop Map utilizes satellite imagery, Artificial intelligence and weather data to deliver hyperlocal, climate-smart farming advice in local languages. Mkulima Plus creates direct market linkages, eliminating exploitative middlemen and ensuring fair prices for farmers. This comprehensive approach helps farmers reduce input waste, increase productivity, increase their profits, and build climate resilience while creating sustainable market opportunities

core_fields.title: How to Produce Aflatoxin-Free Maize and Fortified Maize Flour for Ugandan Consumers (Uganda).
core_fields.description: Agro Supply's ozone technology removes carcinogenic aflatoxins and produces aflatoxin-free fortified flour for local consumers across East African markets.
core_fields.abstract: Mycotoxins pose a global challenge. For example, Uganda continues to experience the long-term impacts of Aflatoxin contamination in grains, which costs the country $38 million annually in missed export opportunities. Aflatoxins endanger the health of the population and threaten food security and livelihoods. Since 2019, Agro Supply has been partnering with smallholder farmers to address issues affecting the East African agricultural value chain. The efforts began with research and seed development, including the distribution of climate-resilient seed varieties for cereal crops and training and establishing an offtake market for over 40,000 smallholder farmers. Currently, we are building a value-added processing facility that cleans and dries grain and removes Aflatoxin through ozonation. Ozonation involves exposing a commodity to ozone, which oxidizes Mycotoxin molecules and renders them non-toxic. Ozone is a strong oxidizing agent that attacks Mycotoxins, transforming harmful molecules into harmless ones. Mycotoxin exposure can happen directly by consuming contaminated food or indirectly through animals that have eaten contaminated feed. Mycotoxins pose serious health risks to humans, ranging from acute poisoning to long-term effects like immune deficiency, malnutrition, stunted growth in children, and cancer. They also create significant economic challenges, causing losses for farmers, grain dealers, and milling companies due to mycotoxin contamination. Besides removing Aflatoxin and providing African manufacturers with clean, Aflatoxin-free grain, we are also milling maize flour and fortifying it with nutritious food nutrients like protein, zinc, and vitamins, then selling it to local consumers in Uganda.

core_fields.title: Biopesticides Innovation and Commercialisation Living Lab (BICoLab)
core_fields.description: We propose a research-led Living Lab to develop, lab- and field-test, and scale five compelling, locally sourced biopesticide formulations. The project will engage farmers, innovators, and SMEs as co-creators through structured incubation, regulatory support, and business development. We aspire to bring at least one tested product to market and establish a national centre for biopesticide technology in Tanzania, thereby laying the foundation for a sustainable, evidence-based agricultural input ecosystem.
core_fields.abstract: The global use of synthetic pesticides in 2023 was 3.73 million tonnes of active ingredient a 71% increase since 2000. Smallholder farmers increasingly rely on these harmful chemicals, risking health, food safety, and environmental integrity, while often overlooking effective, indigenous alternatives like Tephrosia vogelii. Misuse of synthetic pesticides accelerates pest resistance, contaminates ecosystems, and disrupts trade, undermining global goals for sustainable food systems. We propose a Living Lab commercialisation model: a user-centred, innovation ecosystem in which research and development take place in real-life settings, bringing together citizens, businesses, academia, and government to co-create solutions. We will involve farmers, SMEs, researchers, and policymakers to transform indigenous botanical knowledge into standardised, compelling, and locally manufactured biopesticide products. Our model integrates scientific validation, formulation refinement, regulatory navigation, market testing, and business incubation to ensure practical, scalable outcomes. Built on over a decade of multidisciplinary research (Mkindi & Belmain), our team has identified and extracted bioactive compounds (e.g., rotenoids) from T. vogelii, optimised local formulation protocols, and validated their effectiveness in field trials showing comparable efficacy to synthetics while preserving pollinators, beneficial insects, and soil health. Immediate benefits include affordable, safe pest control for farmers, improved crop yields, and safer food for communities. Long-term, the model builds a circular, climate-smart economy with local green manufacturing, reduced environmental contamination, and enhanced biodiversity. By replacing imported chemicals with locally adapted solutions, our Living Lab strengthens food system resilience. It directly supports the transformation toward safer, more sustainable agriculture for both people and the planet.

Our innovation addresses these twin crises by converting organic waste into high-protein fish feed and nutrient-rich biofertilizers through microbial fermentation. Using naturally occurring microbes and industrial biotech processes, we create locally produced, affordable, and sustainable alternatives that reduce dependence on marine resources and chemical fertilizers. This approach is grounded in decades of microbial fermentation research and practical field trials demonstrating improved productivity, cost savings, and environmental resilience. Immediate benefits for farmers include lower feed and fertilizer costs, higher crop yields, and increased fish productivity, directly boosting household incomes. core_fields.title: Scaling hope: How ShopOkoa is redefining financial inclusion and crop insurance for farmers in Kenya.

core_fields.abstract: ShopOkoa addresses the urgent problem of climate risk for smallholder farmers, agri-SMEs, and low-income households, whose livelihoods are increasingly threatened by extreme weather events. Traditional insurance and financial systems are too slow, opaque, and costly to provide meaningful protection, leaving millions of people exposed to crop failure, livestock loss, and income instability. In Africa alone, climate disasters cause over USD 40 billion in annual losses. ShopOkoa solves this by combining AI, satellite-based weather data, and predictive analytics with blockchain-powered parametric insurance. Our platform analyzes climate information in real time, enabling precise risk prediction and dynamic pricing, while smart contracts automate payouts instantly and transparently. Insurance is embedded directly into existing financial networks SACCOs, cooperatives, mobile money, and microfinance institutions ensuring easy accessibility via smartphones, USSD, and insurance cards. The scientific and technical insight driving ShopOkoa is that climate risk can be quantified and acted upon in real time using high-resolution climate data, AI modeling, and decentralized ledger technology. This enables previously uninsurable populations and assets to access reliable protection at low cost. Immediate benefits include stabilizing household income, securing agricultural inputs, and reducing hunger after climate shocks. Sustainable benefits include strengthening financial resilience, enabling asset-based lending, supporting carbon credit development, and building a scalable, transparent climate finance infrastructure. By transforming climate data into actionable risk intelligence, ShopOkoa empowers communities, insurers, and financial institutions to manage climate risk efficiently and equitably.

Immediate benefits include up to 30% improvement in fish yield, 20% reduction in feed and water costs, reduced labor, and better fish survival. Long-term benefits include climate-resilient aquaculture, improved farmer incomes, job creation, reduced environmental pollution, and increased availability of affordable protein for local communities.

core_fields.title: Zero-Waste Fresh Food Ecosystem for Affordable, Nutritious Urban Diets in Nigeria
core_fields.description: Nigeria loses up to half of its fresh produce before it reaches consumers, driving high prices, poor nutrition and environmental waste. This project builds a zero-waste fresh food ecosystem across urban hubs by improving sorting, preservation, value-basket creation, and community redistribution of near-expiry produce. It enables affordable access to nutritious food for low-income families while reducing loss, extending shelf life, and creating circular partnerships for composting and dehydration. The model strengthens diets, sustainability, and food
core_fields.abstract: Nigeria's urban food system suffers from extreme fresh-food losses, up to 40 to 50 percent of vegetables spoil before reaching consumers due to poor sorting, weak handling practices, lack of preservation, and household waste driven by spoilage and limited storage knowledge. This creates high retail prices, volatile supply, and reduced access to nutritious foods for low-income families. Our innovation is a zero-waste fresh food ecosystem built around simple, practical, and scalable interventions that reduce losses at every stage of the supply chain. At our urban hubs, we introduce improved sorting and grading, allowing Grade A produce to move into retail, Grade B into discounted nutrition-value baskets, and Grade C into dehydration or community redistribution. Low-cost preservation methods such as air-drying leafy greens, vegetable dehydration, and improved packaging extend shelf life without expensive equipment. Downstream, households receive portioned produce bundles, storage guides, and use-soon baskets that reduce spoilage and improve affordability. Community redistribution channels ensure near-expiry produce reaches schools, women s groups, and low-income segments rather than being discarded. Circular partnerships with compost producers, animal-feed mixers, and community gardens convert unavoidable waste into productive use. This integrated model delivers immediate benefits: lower food waste, reduced household spending on nutritious foods, better diet diversity, and more stable supply in cities. Long-term, it creates a sustainable, circular food system that strengthens resilience, cuts emissions associated with waste, and improves food security for millions.

core_fields.title: Integrative Metabolomic Profiling of Underutilized Indigenous Crops to Enhance Nutritional Quality and Support Public Health
core_fields.description: This project uses advanced metabolomic and nutritional profiling to uncover health-promoting compounds in underutilized indigenous crops. By integrating sustainable agronomic methods such as organic priming, microbial biocontrol, and nutrient-rich effluent, it aims to enhance crop nutritional quality and support food-based prevention of non-communicable diseases. The findings will inform public health innovation, strengthen local food systems, and build research capacity.
core_fields.abstract: This project introduces a new integrative approach that combines metabolomics, nutritional profiling, and sustainable agronomic practices to enhance the health value of indigenous crops such as Lagenaria siceraria, Vigna subterranea, and Arachis hypogaea. The innovation lies in linking crop biochemical fingerprints directly to public health benefits, something rarely done in current research. Problem Being Solved: South Africa faces a rising burden of non-communicable diseases (NCDs) while traditional, nutrient-rich indigenous crops remain underutilized and poorly understood. Communities increasingly rely on ultra-processed foods, leading to obesity, diabetes, and micronutrient deficiencies. At the same time, smallholder farmers lack low-cost, sustainable methods to improve crop quality and productivity. Relevance: Identifying the bioactive compounds that make indigenous crops nutritious provides scientific evidence needed for dietary guidelines, functional food development, and community health programmes. It also supports climate-resilient agriculture, critical as environmental stresses intensify. How the Problem Is Being Solved: The project uses advanced metabolomic tools (LC-MS/MS, GC-MS, proteomics) to identify the compounds responsible for nutritional and health benefits. These insights are paired with organic seed priming, microbial biocontrol, and aquaculture effluent fertilization, which improve nutrient density and stress tolerance without relying on chemicals or expensive inputs. Scientific Insight Behind the Solution: Recent advances in metabolomics show that plant metabolites directly influence human metabolic health. By profiling these metabolites under different sustainable treatments, the project will identify practical ways to boost crop nutritional quality naturally. With benefits such as; nutrient-dense foods availability and reduced chemical use. Thus, strengthening food security, public health, and climate-smart agriculture simultaneously.

core_fields.title: MoneyMaker FarmTower: A New Generation of Climate-Smart Production
core_fields.description: Africa faces shrinking land access, erratic rainfall, and rising food prices. The MoneyMaker FarmTower is a low-cost vertical growing system that enables year-round production of leafy vegetables using minimal land and water. This project will advance the FarmTower from prototype to market-ready product, validated for mass production and early scaling in Kenya. By creating a new affordability tier for climate-smart assets, it will help smallholder households improve nutrition, income, and climate resilience.
core_fields.abstract: Millions of low-income farmers in Kenya, particularly women and youth, struggle to produce high-value nutritious crops year-round because they lack access to land and reliable water. Existing vertical gardens attempt to fill this gap but fall short. Repurposed maize sacks are cheap and available, yet degrade quickly, lose water through seepage, and produce limited yields. Commercial products remain niche, costly, soil-intensive, laborious to assemble, and lack training support. All lack internal watering mechanisms, causing uneven distribution and crop failure/stunting across the system. These limitations prevent widespread adoption and a scalable retail model. KickStart's MoneyMaker FarmTower introduces a purpose-built, affordable, and mass-producible vertical garden solution. Drawing on human-centered design, agronomy, and farmer feedback, it offers high-impact innovations: - Form Factor: Conical structure enables sun-exposure across system. It requires less soil, and the top tier serves as a seedling nursery, eliminating the need for external germination beds. - Internal Watering System: Central column distributes water evenly and reduces evaporation. - Production Capacity: Grows 100+ leafy vegetable plants in one sq-meter. - Assembly: Pop-up frame allows a single user set-up in 20 minutes. - Training: Complementary visual guides and digital training videos to support success. This product enables climate-vulnerable farmers to conserve more water, using ~20% of the water required for open-field production. At a target retail price of $10 USD, the FarmTower offers low-income farmers, including youth and women, a significant ROI of USD $1.50-3 in weekly income per unit, creating a practical entry point into year-round, climate-resilient food production.

core_fields.title: Building Digital Agriculture Skills for Marginalized Farmers in Lucknow, India
core_fields.description: Marginalized farmers lack digital skills for modern food markets. We will train 300 underprivileged agricultural workers in computer basics, e-commerce platforms, and agricultural technology over 18 months. Participants gain income-generating skills, market information access, and improved food security. This initiative bridges digital divides, strengthens food system participation, and creates sustainable livelihoods while establishing a replicable community training model.
core_fields.abstract: Challenge & Opportunity Underprivileged agricultural communities in Lucknow remain trapped in traditional market systems, unable to access modern food economy opportunities. This digital exclusion perpetuates poverty cycles, limits income growth, and threatens food security. Yet technology offers transformative potential for marginalized farmers and agricultural workers seeking economic advancement. Project Solution Our 18-month initiative trains 300 vulnerable agricultural workers in essential digital competencies. We combine foundational computer literacy with practical agricultural technology, e-commerce expertise, and market-access tools. Training occurs in community settings, eliminating geographic and financial obstacles to participation. Curriculum & Methodology Our evidence-based curriculum covers computer fundamentals, digital safety, agricultural apps and platforms, e-commerce operations, and online payment systems. Instruction emphasizes hands-on learning through real market scenarios. Participants practice using actual agricultural platforms, accessing genuine market data, and conducting digital transactions. Direct Outcomes Participants gain immediate, income-generating capabilities. They access previously unavailable market information, negotiate better prices, and reduce intermediary exploitation. Digital skills enable direct customer connections, expanding revenue opportunities while ensuring food security through increased agricultural profitability. Systemic Impact This project transforms food system participation for excluded populations. Trained individuals become community technology ambassadors, creating cascading adoption effects. Enhanced digital literacy strengthens local agricultural markets, improves supply chain efficiency, and builds resilient food systems. Sustainability & Scale Peer-to-peer knowledge transfer ensures lasting impact beyond project funding. Community networks provide ongoing support. Success creates demand for expanded training, establishing foundation for scaled implementation across Uttar Pradesh.

core_fields.title: Women-Led Smart Urban Farming Innovation Project in Akaki Kality Sub-City, Addis Ababa, Ethiopia.
core_fields.description: Seeds of Hope: Women-Led Smart Urban Farming Innovation Project empowers destitute single mothers and young women through small-space, scientific urban agriculture. Using efficient, climate-smart methods, participants grow high-value vegetables and process produce in micro-agro units. The project strengthens food security, generates stable income, and creates a sustainable profit-sharing model. With seed funding, Muday Charity Association will expand innovative urban farming hubs that transform livelihoods and promote equitable, resilient local food systems.
core_fields.abstract: Seeds of Hope introduces a smart, small-space urban farming model designed to empower destitute single mothers and young women while strengthening local food systems. The innovation addresses two urgent challenges: limited access to nutritious food in low-income urban areas and the lack of sustainable livelihoods for vulnerable women. Traditional farming requires large land and high inputs, which are not accessible in densely populated urban settings. Muday Charity Association s solution replaces this barrier with a compact, scientifically guided micro-agriculture system. The innovation uses climate-smart techniques such as vertical growing towers, container farming, organic composting from household waste, and efficient water-saving irrigation. These methods increase yields using minimal land and resources. The approach is informed by urban agriculture research demonstrating that controlled micro-environments can reduce crop loss, enhance nutritional quality, and extend year-round production. Women are trained to manage micro-plots and small agro-processing units that convert vegetables into marketable products such as sauces, dried greens, and packaged produce. This creates dual income streams fresh produce sales and value-added products while establishing a cooperative, profit-sharing structure managed by the women themselves. Immediate benefits include improved household nutrition, reduced food expenses, and new income opportunities for participants. Communities benefit from increased availability of affordable, fresh produce. Environmentally, the model reduces waste through composting, promotes regenerative practices, lowers chemical inputs, and maximizes land efficiency. Sustainably, the project builds long-term skills, strengthens local food systems, and enables women to become independent micro-entrepreneurs contributing to resilient urban economies.

core_fields.title: Black Soldier Fly Farming: Transforming waste into a valuable protein source.
core_fields.description: RaL Farmstead seeks to expand its Black Soldier Fly innovation, which transforms organic waste into affordable, high-protein animal feed and organic fertilizer. This reduces livestock feed costs for farmers while enhancing soil health and waste management in local communities. The innovation enhances food security, creates green jobs for youths, and supports the circular economy. Having a working prototype, the project is ready to scale and deliver direct economic and environmental benefits to Malawian farming communities.
core_fields.abstract: RaL Farmstead innovation uses Black Soldier Fly (BSF) to convert organic waste into high-quality livestock feed and organic fertilizer. This solution directly addresses two major challenges faced by the Malawian food system, which are the rising cost of livestock feed and the poor management of organic waste in communities. The problem is relevant now more than ever. A report by CIMMYT (2024) reveals that feed prices account for up to 70% of livestock production costs, limiting profitability for smallholder farmers and constraining growth in poultry, piggery, and aquaculture sectors. At the same time, communities struggle with waste pollution and poor soil health, which reduces crop productivity and compromises food security. RaL Farmstead solves these challenges by applying proven biological and circular economy principles. BSF larvae rapidly consume organic waste and convert it into protein biomass containing essential proteins. Scientific studies show BSF can reduce organic waste volume by up to 85.5% (Anokye, 2025) while producing high-quality feed and biofertilizer. This makes BSF farming a climate-smart and resource-efficient alternative to conventional feed production and chemical fertilizers. The immediate benefits include lower feed costs for farmers, safer and cleaner communities through waste reduction, and access to affordable organic fertilizer for improved crop yields. In the long term, the innovation supports rural job creation, strengthens local food value chains, decreases dependence on imported feed, and contributes to environmental sustainability. We position Malawi to unlock economic opportunities in the growing global insect protein market while empowering young farmers and communities with resilient, eco-friendly resources.

core_fields.title: Fortified, Shelf-Stable Food Innovation to Transform School Nutrition Systems
core_fields.description: This project establishes a climate-resilient, centralized nutrition manufacturing system in Remuna, Odisha, to produce fortified, millet-based, long shelf-life morning foods for underserved schoolchildren. Using a hub-and-spoke distribution model, it delivers safe, nutrient-dense snacks such as chikkis, millet bars, and roasted protein mixes to address early-morning hunger and enhance learning readiness. The scalable model strengthens local value chains, reduces food waste, and expands equitable access to sustainable, affordable child nutrition.
core_fields.abstract: Millions of children in India begin their school day without breakfast, impairing concentration, attendance, and long-term learning outcomes. Existing meal systems rely on perishable foods, limiting the ability to reach remote schools early in the day. This innovation introduces a climate-smart, fortified, shelf-stable food manufacturing system designed to overcome these barriers. The Remuna facility applies food science, engineering, and fortification technology to create culturally familiar, ready-to-eat products such as millet cookies, peanut and ragi chikkis, energy bars, and micronutrient-enriched jaggery cubes that remain safe and nutrient-stable for 2 3 months. These products deliver protein, iron, calcium, omega-3 fats, and essential vitamins in formats tailored to children s preferences while meeting rigorous safety and quality standards. A key systems innovation is the hub-and-spoke distribution model: Remuna serves as the manufacturing hub, while existing Akshaya Patra kitchens across Odisha operate as spokes to reach remote schools efficiently, reducing logistics costs, waste, and variability in nutrition delivery. By using climate-resilient millets and locally sourced pulses, the system strengthens farmer livelihoods and supports regenerative agricultural practices. Immediate benefits include improved morning nutrition, enhanced classroom attentiveness, and reduced hunger. Long-term benefits include supply-chain resilience, reduced food loss, rural employment, and a scalable model that can transform child nutrition delivery across India. This approach integrates science, sustainability, and equity to reshape school feeding systems.

core_fields.title: Scaling Portable Solar-Powered Agri Sprayers to Improve Productivity for Smallholder Farmers in Rural Ethiopia
core_fields.description: This project scales a solar-powered sprayer already developed and field-tested at Arba Minch University s Renewable Energy Centre(university agriculture farm). The system reduces the physical strain of manual spraying and improves crop protection for poor smallholder farmers in rural Ethiopia. Seed Grant funding will support building 50 units, training farmers in safe use, aware of natural farming practices , maintenance, and generating evidence on cost, labor savings, and yield gains for future scale-up.
core_fields.abstract: Smallholder farmers in rural Ethiopia still rely on manual sprayers or even leaves to apply pesticides or organic pest solutions. These traditional methods demand intense physical effort, deliver uneven coverage, waste inputs, and expose farmers to pests and disease outbreaks. As a result, productivity falls, input costs rise, and food security remains fragile for already vulnerable households. The innovation is a solar-powered agricultural sprayer developed at Arba Minch University s Renewable Energy Centre, which is well recognized for electrifying rural villages, schools, and health centers through its solar programs. Building on a successful battery-powered sprayer that received community service recognition, the team engineered a fully solar-driven unit that eliminates manual pumping and grid dependency. The sprayer integrates a compact solar module, charge controller, rechargeable battery, ergonomic 20-liter tank, and a high-pressure adjustable nozzle capable of spraying up to 10 meters. Its design was refined through field testing and farmer consultations in Lante village, where the key insight was clear: farmers need mechanization that is affordable, off-grid, easy to maintain, and powerful enough for tall crops like mango and coffee. The solution immediately reduces labor burden, improves spray accuracy, lowers chemical waste, and increases the speed of farm operations. Long-term benefits include higher yields, reduced production costs, safer fertilizer handling, and stronger household resilience. Because the sprayer is locally manufactured at the Renewable Energy Centre, the initiative also builds indigenous engineering capacity and supports the growth of rural clean-energy enterprises with lasting benefits for farmers, communities, and the environment.

core_fields.title: Solar-Powered Irrigation and Regenerative Agriculture for Climate-Resilient Food Systems of Kayumbu watershed in Rwanda
core_fields.description: The project addresses climate vulnerability and food insecurity affecting 500 smallholder farmers in Kayumbu Watershed caused by rain-fed farming and land degradation. It deploys solar-powered irrigation, regenerative land management, and nutrition-sensitive agriculture to enable year-round production on 5 hectares. Expected outputs include 20-40% yield increases and restored soils. The project will improve nutrition, raise incomes by 20%, and benefit 10,000+ community members, especially women and youth.
core_fields.abstract: Smallholder farmers in Kayumbu Watershed, IN Rwanda Southern Province, Kamonyi District, rely on rainfall, making them highly vulnerable to drought, soil erosion, and declining food production. This innovation introduces a solar-powered irrigation and regenerative agriculture model that enables continuous production of nutritious crops while restoring degraded landscapes. The solution integrates renewable energy for water pumping, efficient irrigation technologies, climate-smart farming practices, and watershed rehabilitation. This approach simultaneously increases food availability, improves dietary diversity, reduces environmental degradation, and enhances household livelihoods. Unlike traditional irrigation systems that rely unpredictable rainfall, this model uses solar energy, making it affordable, sustainable, and resilient to climate change. The scientific and technical foundation includes solar photovoltaic pumping, soil-water conservation engineering, agroforestry systems, and nutrition-sensitive crop diversification. Regenerative practices, mulching, terracing, composting, and contour bunds, restore soil fertility, sequester carbon, and improve water retention, keeping food systems within planetary boundaries. Immediate benefits include reliable water access, higher yields, reduced hunger months, and improved income for farmers. Sustainable long-term benefits include restored ecosystems, reduced food loss during drought, affordable nutritious foods in local markets, empowered women and youth, and greater resilience to climate shocks. The innovation directly benefits farmers, households, schools, cooperatives, consumers, and the wider environment, offering a scalable model for Rwanda and similar countries like Uganda, Tanzania, Kenya, DRC, and Burundi.
